name: Goan Konkani
notes: Goan Konkani (गोंयची कोंकणी / Gõychi Konknni), the official language of Goa, India (Konkani Official Language Act, 1987) written in Devanagari (the constitutionally recognised script for the Eighth-Schedule language 'Konkani'); ~2.3 million speakers across the wider Konkani-speaking area. Konkani is exceptional in being officially written in several scripts (Devanagari, Latin 'Romi Konkani', Kannada, Malayalam); this spec covers the DEVANAGARI rendering only. GRAPHEMES: the Devanagari letter-to-sound conventions are read the SAME way Hindi's spec already encodes them (`graphemes_base: hi`), following the `doi`/`mag`/`new` precedent in this dataset -- a claim about the shared script's reading convention, not about Konkani's own phonology (which differs from Hindi's, e.g. Konkani's nasal vowels and the /d̪ʒ/-/tʃ/ contrasts described by Almeida 1989). KNOWN GAP: Konkani's phonemic vowel nasalisation and its distinct treatment of schwa-deletion environments (compared to Hindi's) are not yet split out as Konkani-specific overrides -- left undone rather than guessed, a documented gap. STRESS: Almeida (1989) does not describe a lexical stress contrast for Konkani; left unencoded, a documented exemption. TIER: no WikiPron (or other registrable) gold exists for `gom` (checked against CUNY-CL/wikipron's scrape summary, 2026-08-03: zero rows), so `skeleton`, not `research`.
